historical_references.reference: Ibn Rushd, also known as Averroes, wrote a commentary on Aristotle's Metaphysics in Arabic, which he entitled 'The Decisive Treatise'. In this work, he gave the name 'Muqaddimah' to the introductory section, which served as a summary of the essentials of Aristotelian philosophy and as an introduction to Aristotle's Metaphysics. This name was later adopted for Ibn Rushd's comprehensive work 'The Major Commentary on Aristotle's Metaphysics'.

The term 'Muqaddimah' or 'Mugaddasah' (Arabic: ابن التقديم, 'The Preface') was also used by Ibn Khaldun in the title of his magnum opus, 'The Muqaddimah'. In this work, Ibn Khaldun provided a comprehensive history of the world, starting from the creation of the universe until the time of his writing in the 14th century. The Muqaddimah is considered a seminal work in the fields of history, sociology, and economics, and it covers various topics, including the cycles of civilization.

Scholars in these fields often refer to a 'Muqaddim' as an author who provides an extensive and comprehensive introduction to their work. The 'Muqaddimah' serves as a foundation for the main text, providing necessary background information and context. In the modern context, the term 'Muqaddim' is commonly seen in academic journals, scholarly conferences, and online learning platforms. Scholars publish their research in academic journals, often including a 'Muqaddimah' to provide context and background information for their findings. In scholarly conferences, presenters may reference a 'Muqaddimah' or an influential scholar's work to provide context for their own research. Online learning platforms, such as Khan Academy and Coursera, also utilize the 'Muqaddimah' concept by providing comprehensive introductions to various subjects before delving into the main content. Overall, the 'Muqaddim' concept is a crucial part of modern Islamic scholarship, serving to provide necessary context and background information for academic research and learning.
